newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Games to be played over the weekend in the Spanish first division: (current league standings in brackets, kick off times gmt)
Seven former Real reserve team players line up for this year's surprise outfit against their old club in a match which the leaders need to win to guarantee spending New Year on top.
Athletic midfielder Julen Guerrero returns after scoring all three goals in Spain's win over Malta midweek for what is, on paper, the most straightforward game of the weekend.
Barcelona have only let four points escape them in the Camp Nou but have had a troublesome fortnight of dressing-room conflict after their defeat by Real Madrid.
Deportivo's John Toshack hopes to have new signings Renaldo and Helder ready to face a Sporting side where former Real Madrid coach Benito Floro is struggling to keep his job.
Logrones have struggled with only two victories at home, while Rayo have surprised the pundits and have managed to bring points home from half of their away games.
Compostela haven't won at home since beating champions Atletico Madrid in the second game of the season, and like their opponents badly need a boost ahead of the New Year break.
Former Real Madrid man Miguel Soler is set to make his debut in place of suspended defender Kily Gonzalez as Zaragoza try to clock up what would be only their second home win of the season.
After going seven games without defeat Atletico but have been hit by injuries and the suspension of Diego Simeone. But fellow midfielder Jose Luis Caminero may be fit to play.
Espanyol will be hoping to repeat last season's 4-1 win at Tenerife, who are without injured striker Meho Kodro and midfielders Slavisa Jokanovic and Dani Gonzalez.
Sevilla have only won one game at home, while Betis are yet to lose away. But the form book tends to get thrown to the winds in the big Seville derby game.
Newly-promoted Hercules of Alicante play their first derby game in the top flight for eleven years against a Valencia side boosted by the arrival of Brazilian forward Leandro.
